01

Executive Summary

This project investigates sex-driven differences in gene expression across three clinically relevant human tissues using GTEx v8 transcriptomic data, examining whether sex-biased genes contribute to documented disparities in the prevalence and progression of atherosclerosis, breast cancer, and Alzheimer's disease.

Working entirely in R (RStudio v4.4.1), the project combined data harmonisation, gene-wise linear regression modelling across approximately 19,000 variables per tissue, multiple testing correction (Benjamini-Hochberg and Bonferroni), GWAS Catalogue orthogonal analysis (Fisher's Exact Test), KEGG pathway enrichment (clusterProfiler and DAVID), and genome-wide statistical visualisation in ggplot2.

Analysis of 1,088 samples across three tissues — spanning approximately 21 million data points — identified 801 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) in aorta artery and 5,597 DEGs in breast mammary tissue. Five KEGG pathways reached statistical significance in breast tissue (DAVID, BH-adjusted), all enriched in female-upregulated genes.

The brain hippocampus yielded only 13 DEGs — reflecting the smaller sample size (n=197) and male-skewed cohort (73% male) — and was not advanced to pathway analysis. This is an acknowledged study limitation and a direction for future research.

02

End-to-End Analytical Workflow

A reproducible six-stage pipeline designed and executed entirely in R, from raw GTEx data acquisition to pathway-level biological interpretation.

STEP 01
Data Acquisition
Downloaded GTEx v8 TPM expression matrices, phenotype metadata (age, sex, death classification) and genomic annotation files for three tissues.
STEP 02
Harmonisation & QC
Validated and matched subject identifiers (SUBJID), trimmed whitespace, filtered unexpressed genes, and merged expression with phenotype data.
STEP 03
Differential Expression
Fitted gene-wise linear regression models (lm) across ~19,000 genes per tissue. Wilcoxon non-parametric test applied to brain hippocampus where regression assumptions were violated.
STEP 04
Multiple Testing Correction
Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction for aorta and brain; Bonferroni for breast mammary where the larger DEG count justified greater stringency.
STEP 05
Annotation & GWAS Mapping
Mapped Ensembl IDs to gene symbols via biomaRt; Fisher's Exact Test to assess DEG overlap with GWAS Catalogue disease-associated genes.
STEP 06
Pathway Enrichment
KEGG pathway enrichment using clusterProfiler (aorta) and DAVID (breast); visualised with bar charts, volcano plots, and Manhattan plots in ggplot2.

Genes on sex chromosomes X and Y were excluded to focus analysis on autosomal differential expression, minimising sex-specific copy-number biases. Protein-coding genes were the most abundant class across all three tissues. All analyses were conducted on pseudonymised public GTEx v8 data (gtexportal.org).

04

Statistical Visualisations

Six visualisation types produced across three tissues, combining genome-wide signal mapping, effect-size-significance plots, and distribution diagnostics — all generated in ggplot2 (R).

Figure A — Breast Mammary Tissue
Volcano plot: Beta coefficient (effect size) on x-axis; −log₁₀(p-value) on y-axis. Female-upregulated genes (rose, positive beta) dominate the significant signal. Dashed line = Bonferroni threshold.
Figure B — Genome-Wide Signal (Aorta & Breast)
Manhattan plots: Each point is one gene, positioned by chromosomal location. Taller peaks = stronger statistical evidence. Both tissues show significant signal across multiple chromosomes.
Figure C — P-Value Distribution (All 3 Tissues)
P-value histograms: A pronounced peak near zero in aorta and breast confirms genuine sex-biased signal. Brain hippocampus shows a near-uniform distribution, consistent with the low DEG count (13).
Figure D — Gene Type Distribution (All 3 Tissues)
Gene type composition: Protein-coding genes are the dominant class in all three tissues. Breast has the widest gene type variety. lincRNA and processed pseudogenes also feature prominently.
Figure E — Top DEG Expression by Sex (All 3 Tissues)
Boxplots: Expression distribution of the most significant differentially expressed gene per tissue, stratified by sex. Female samples show wider distributions; male samples show tighter, centred distributions.
Figure F — Top KEGG Pathways · Aorta (Female-Upregulated)
Pathway enrichment (clusterProfiler, BH-adjusted): Top enriched KEGG pathways in female-upregulated aorta DEGs. Point size = gene count; colour = −log₁₀(adj.p). Dashed line = FDR 0.05 threshold.

Results & Key Findings

Methodological note

Bonferroni correction was applied to breast tissue because the BH method yielded 13,245 DEGs — too large a set for meaningful pathway enrichment. Bonferroni's greater stringency produced a more tractable 5,597-gene set. Brain hippocampus was not advanced to pathway analysis due to the very low DEG count, likely caused by the smaller sample size and male-skewed cohort.

GWAS Orthogonal Analysis

Tissue ↔ DiseaseOdds Ratiop-value
Aorta ↔ Atherosclerosis1.120.683 (n.s.)
Breast ↔ Breast Cancer1.150.084 (n.s.)

Odds ratios slightly above 1.0 suggest a weak positive trend, but confidence intervals include 1.0, precluding a statistically significant conclusion. This indicates that sex-biased DEGs in these tissues are not substantially enriched in known GWAS-associated disease genes — a scientifically valid negative finding.

06

Statistically Significant KEGG Pathways

Pathway enrichment analysis (DAVID, Fisher's Exact Test with Benjamini-Hochberg correction) identified five statistically significant pathways in breast mammary tissue, all enriched in female-upregulated genes.

Aorta artery clusterProfiler analysis identified additional significant pathways (Ribosome, Coronavirus Disease, Dopaminergic Synapse, and others) in female-upregulated DEGs as shown in Figure F above. No pathways were taken forward for brain hippocampus.

01
ECM-Receptor Interaction
Extracellular matrix components and integrin-mediated signalling are established drivers of breast cancer cell adhesion, migration, and proliferation. Female-higher expression is consistent with oestrogen's role in modulating ECM composition and receptor signalling.
BH-adjusted · breast
02
Cell Adhesion Molecules
Cell adhesion molecules act as tumour suppressors through contact inhibition. Sex-biased dysregulation — enriched in females — disrupts this function and facilitates uncontrolled cell growth and metastasis, relevant to breast cancer pathophysiology.
BH-adjusted · breast
03
Viral Protein Interaction with Cytokine and Cytokine Receptor
Cytokine-mediated immune signalling is central to the tumour microenvironment. Female-enriched expression may indicate heightened immune responsiveness or susceptibility to viral oncogenesis — consistent with evidence linking HPV and EBV to breast cancer.
BH-adjusted · breast
04
Coronavirus Disease – COVID-19
Enrichment reflects overlap between SARS-CoV-2 host interaction genes and sex-biased immune regulation in breast tissue, consistent with documented sex differences in COVID-19 immune response and shared cytokine receptor pathways.
BH-adjusted · breast
05
Basal Cell Carcinoma
Enrichment in a cancer-related proliferation pathway with higher expression in females further supports the hypothesis that sex-specific gene expression is a biological driver — not merely a consequence — of differential cancer susceptibility between sexes.
BH-adjusted · breast
Key Biological Conclusion

The concentration of significant pathways in breast mammary tissue — particularly ECM-Receptor Interaction, Cell Adhesion Molecules, and Cytokine signalling — supports the hypothesis that sex-biased gene expression is an intrinsic driver of breast cancer sex disparities, rather than merely a consequence of disease. This finding is consistent with the study's primary hypothesis that genes influenced by sex differences also contribute to the prevalence differences between men and women.

Analytical Competencies Demonstrated

The technical skills deployed in this project map directly onto core competencies expected of information analysts, data analysts, and health data scientists across NHS, public sector, and research environments.

⚙️
Data Engineering & Pipeline Design
Merged high-dimensional expression matrices, phenotype metadata, and genomic annotation files across multiple sources with identifier reconciliation, whitespace standardisation, and validation at each stage.
📐
Statistical Modelling & Multiple Testing
Applied gene-wise linear regression across 19,000+ variables, selecting correction methods (BH vs Bonferroni) based on DEG count and analytical purpose — balancing sensitivity and specificity.
🔗
Data Source Reconciliation
Integrated three independent data sources (GTEx expression, phenotype metadata, GWAS Catalogue) with Ensembl-to-symbol ID mapping via biomaRt and contingency table construction for Fisher's Exact Test.
📈
Visual Analytics & Communication
Produced volcano plots, Manhattan plots, p-value distribution histograms, gene type bar charts, boxplots, and pathway enrichment charts in ggplot2 — communicating complex high-dimensional outputs clearly.
🧪
Hypothesis Testing & Inference
Designed and executed orthogonal validation using Fisher's Exact Test between DEG lists and GWAS-identified disease genes; interpreted odds ratios, confidence intervals, and p-values to draw robust, qualified conclusions.
📝
Evidence-Based Reporting
Translated statistically complex outputs into clear, interpretable conclusions with biological context — a critical skill for producing intelligence products in public health, policy, and NHS analytical roles.
